findings.title: Translation cache key ignores the site-dependent fallback chain
findings.body:
The LRU cache key is built only from key, `config.locale` and the backend object_id. With the new Fallbacks module, the value returned for a locale also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which `FallbackLocaleList#[]` reads on every lookup. That setting differs per site in multisite and can be changed by an admin at runtime.

The cache is process-wide, so the first fallback result is stored and reused for everyone. Example: an `:es` user on site A (default `:fr`) hits a key missing in `es`, and the French text is cached. An `:es` user on site B (default `:de`) then gets French instead of German. After an admin changes `default_locale`, stale fallback text is served until `I18n.reload!`.

A 'translation missing' result, or an `en` result produced before the site locale was loaded, is also cached permanently. The cache key should include the fallback chain (or at least `SiteSetting.default_locale`), or fallback results should not be cached.

findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded in the controller before_filter
findings.body:
Translations are lazy-loaded per locale. `translate` only calls `load_locale(config.locale)`. The fallback locales (site default and `:en`) are loaded only by `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` in `ApplicationController#set_locale`.

Any code path that translates outside a controller request gets no loaded fallbacks. That includes Sidekiq jobs, mailers run from jobs, rake tasks, and code that sets `I18n.locale` or uses `I18n.with_locale`. When `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` iterates over those unloaded locales it finds nothing and returns 'translation missing'. Because of the LRU cache, that result is then stuck for the process.

The fallback chain should be ensured inside `translate` (e.g. `I18n.fallbacks[config.locale].each { |l| ensure_loaded!(l) }`) rather than only in a controller filter.

findings.title: FallbackLocaleList does not normalize locale to a symbol
findings.body:
`I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` normally calls `to_sym` on the locale it is given; this replacement does not. When a caller passes `locale: 'en'` (a String), the result is `['en', :fr, :en]`. `uniq` does not remove the duplicate, so the same locale is looked up twice.

In `ensure_loaded!` a string locale would also miss the `@loaded_locales.include?` check, which stores symbols. Use `[locale.to_sym, ...]` (guarding for nil) before `uniq`.
